text: If your web designer disappeared tomorrow, could you still change your own website?
For a lot of small businesses, the honest answer is no.
Because the designer bought the domain, set up the hosting, and kept every login.
So you're paying for a website you don't actually control.
Here are three things you should own, in your own name.
One. Your domain, that's your web address. Register it to your business, with a login you can get into.
If it's in someone else's account and a renewal gets missed, your website and your email can stop working.
Two. Your hosting, where the website actually lives. Get your own account, or at least admin access.
Three. The admin login for the website itself, plus your Google Business Profile and analytics.
Asking for these isn't rude. It's your business, and a good web person will happily hand them over.
